workstream: WS8 — cross-family judge panels (P4) + instrument-clarity builtin check (gap 3)
summary: Implements the one true prescription gap (P4) plus the Sec 10.2 instrument-clarity recipe. (1) judges[].model accepts a LIST (string stays valid, backcompat byte-identical): config normalizes the list into JudgeConfig.model (primary = first entry, keeps every existing consumer working — score.py:1714 _resolve_judge_model, cmd_pairwise:2804) plus a derived JudgeConfig.panel_models list. (2) score_cases fans the LLM-judge call out per model via a _PanelScorer facade; k samples run PER MODEL (samples × models calls), each model's k draws are reduced first by the existing _aggregate_samples (score.py:1190) so within-model self-consistency is never conflated with inter-rater agreement; the injected per-case verdict is then a second literal _aggregate_samples pass over the per-model reduced records (strict-majority bool with ties→fail, median_low numeric — exactly aligned by construction). The cross-family IRR matrix for reliability.krippendorff_alpha is cases × models over per-model REDUCED ratings, with errored/off-scale models as missing ratings (never a nominal category — V3-1 verdict correction 5). (3) Family composition via a conservative prefix heuristic (infer_model_family, silent None on unrecognized/gateway aliases), a cross_family/within-family/unknown label on every alpha (V3-1 correction 6 analog: within-family alpha is labeled 'may be spuriously high — P4', never claimed as cross-family), a config-load warnings.warn when ≥2 explicitly configured role/judge models all resolve to ONE recognized family (Appendix B.4), and a min_panel_alpha threshold key in detect_regressions where perfect-agreement degenerate matrices PASS (V3-1 correction 1) and the Harbor path strips reliability keys with a stderr note (V3-1 correction 2; harbor aggregation at results.py:574-581 carries no panel data while the in-container verifier at harbor/reward.py:221-226 does run score_cases). Panel/clarity results merge into summary['judges'][name] — never a top-level-only block — so cmd_regression, report.py:1309 and log_results (which all call the same detector, per tests/test_threshold_consumers.py) see them with zero extra wiring (V3-2 verdict correction 1). (4) Instrument clarity ships as a score.py SUBCOMMAND (`score.py clarity`), not a builtin judge (builtins run per-case inside score_cases and cannot compute a cross-case coefficient or take a model panel) and not an eval-analyze step (rubric clarity is only measurable against real run outputs; eval-analyze runs pre-execution): ≥2 (recommended 3) cross-family raters + the run's recorded verdict as incumbent rater re-rate an N≤20 stratified, seed-deterministic case subsample with the judge's own rendered rubric; k-way Krippendorff alpha vs the literature-backed 0.67, with sampling basis recorded (V3-2 correction 4) and a small-N floor below which only the raw table is emitted (V3-2 spirit). MULTI-PROVIDER, stated precisely (not hand-waved): the ONLY LLM-judge client is _get_anthropic_client (score.py:2328-2344) — anthropic.Anthropic honoring ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, or AnthropicVertex; every judge call is client.messages.create with forced tool_choice (score.py:1047-1055). Therefore ALL panel members route through one endpoint: non-Anthropic families are reachable only via an Anthropic-Messages-compatible gateway (e.g. a LiteLLM proxy serving /v1/messages with aliases like gpt-4o/gemini-2.5-pro and translating forced tool calls), configured by pointing ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL at it; with a bare Anthropic key the panel is necessarily within-family and the report labels it so. No native OpenAI/Gemini SDK path is added; the mlflow make_judge fallback (score.py:2076-2096, active only when no Anthropic creds exist) raises a clear error for panel judges. WS8 has no direct verdict in /tmp/wf-layers.json (P4 was the un-designed gap); the closest analogous corrections from the V3-1, V3-2 and V2-3 verdicts are incorporated as itemized above and in the per-file specs.
depends_on: WS-V3-1 (agent_eval/reliability.py): krippendorff_alpha(units, level) -> (value|None, reason) — pure stdlib, missing-data tolerant, degenerate zero-variance -> (None, 'perfect agreement...'), insufficient-data floor (<2 units with >=2 ratings). WS8 calls it at two sites (panel aggregation, cmd_clarity) and ADDS infer_model_family to the same module. If sequencing forces WS8 first, WS8 must create agent_eval/reliability.py with exactly this krippendorff_alpha subset per V3-1's spec and V3-1 extends it later (adapt at the two call sites if V3-1 lands with a different signature).

Gateway availability is an ops prerequisite, not a code dependency: cross-family panels need an Anthropic-Messages-compatible proxy (LiteLLM) reachable via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL; within-family panels work with a bare Anthropic key and are honestly labeled.

changes.spec: ADD (to WS-V3-1's module; if WS8 lands first, create the module with V3-1's krippendorff_alpha contract too): infer_model_family(model_id: str) -> Optional[str]. Conservative provider-family inference: (1) s = model_id.strip().lower(); (2) vendor-dot tokens checked against the FULL string first for Bedrock-style ids ('anthropic.' or '.anthropic.' -> 'anthropic'; same for 'meta.', 'mistral.', 'cohere.', 'amazon.'); (3) otherwise take the segment after the last '/' (strips LiteLLM route prefixes like 'openai/gpt-4o', 'vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-pro') and prefix-match a small table: claude->anthropic; regex ^(gpt-|chatgpt|o[134](?:-|$)) -> openai (regex-anchored so 'olmo' is NOT matched); gemini->google; llama/meta-llama->meta; mistral/mixtral/ministral/magistral/codestral->mistral; qwen->alibaba; deepseek->deepseek; grok->xai; command->cohere; nova->amazon. (4) Anything else -> None. Docstring states the contract callers must honor: None means 'unknown — stay silent, never warn, never claim single- or cross-family' (V2-3 correction: the heuristic must fail silent on gateway aliases, never false-positive). Pure stdlib (re only). Module stays importable from config.py at load time.

(2) _load_llm_judge (2030-2099): refactor the Anthropic-path closure into an inner def _make(model): returning the existing scorer body with model bound (rendered prompt/_extract_images/_call_structured_judge unchanged); return _PanelScorer(jc.panel_models, _make) when jc.panel_models else the single scorer with scorer.for_model = _make attached (cmd_clarity reuses it for arbitrary rater models). On the mlflow make_judge fallback branch (2076-2096): if jc.panel_models -> raise RuntimeError('judge panels require the Anthropic client path (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN/Vertex), optionally through an Anthropic-compatible gateway via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL'). (3) _make_builtin_scorer llm-kind branch (806-822): same _make(model) refactor + _PanelScorer/for_model treatment (builtin LLM judges are bool-only and load_judges pins their samples to 1 at 785-790 — panels still work with 1 draw/model; documented). (4) NEW _score_panel(scorer, rec, models, n_samples, bounds, name, judge_type, case_id) -> per-case record dict, called from _score_case's judge loop (insert a panel branch before the n>1 branch at 1582: panel = getattr(scorer, 'panel_models', None)). Per model: run n_samples draws through scorer.for_model(m), each _normalize_result + _enforce_bounds (off-scale -> error sample, per-judge bounds from the existing judge_bounds map); reduce the k draws with _aggregate_samples(runs, judge_type) when n_samples>1 else runs[0]. Cross-model reduction: literally call _aggregate_samples over the per-model reduced records ({value, rationale, error} per model) — guarantees strict-majority-bool-ties-fail / median_low-numeric alignment; majority is over models that produced a rating (errored models shrink the rater pool, matching existing semantics); all models errored -> {value: None, error, ...}. Result record: {value, rationale (from a model matching the reduced value), judge_type, panel: {models, samples_per_model, ratings: {model: reduced value or None}, errors: {model: msg} for errored only, families: {model: infer_model_family(m) or None}, per_model_stability: {model: {values, error_count, stable}} only when n_samples>1}}. Also ALWAYS emit sample_rationales = [{value, rationale: '[<model>] <text>', error}] per model so report.py's existing per-case tab renderer (2651-2670) shows per-model rationales with zero report changes. Deliberately NO top-level 'stability' key on panel records (model disagreement is not sampling instability; keeps the cross-case stable_cases block at 1662-1676 from conflating the two). (5) score_cases cross-case aggregation: after the stability block (1676), for each judge whose per-case records carry 'panel': models list read from config (config.judges), not from the first scored case (V3-1 correction 8 analog); build the cases × models matrix from panel.ratings with None = missing (errored/off-scale models are missing ratings, NOT a category — V3-1 correction 5); level: bool values -> 'nominal', declared int score_range (judge_bounds is_int) -> 'ordinal', float -> 'interval', undeclared numeric -> ordinal iff all observed ints else interval; alpha, reason = reliability.krippendorff_alpha(units, level). aggregated[name]['panel'] = {models, n_models, families, cross_family: True|False|None (None when any family unknown — never claimed), alpha, alpha_metric: f'krippendorff_alpha_{level}', n_units, reason (when alpha None), label: 'cross-family inter-judge agreement' | 'within-family inter-judge agreement (may be spuriously high — P4)' | 'family composition unknown (unrecognized model ids)', per_model: {model: {mean|pass_rate over that model's ratings}} (per-rater marginal = the bias observable)}. No Landis-Koch labels anywhere. Flows into summary['judges'] via the existing _merge_summary at 2741-2745 (the values-stripping dict comp keeps 'panel' — only 'values' is dropped). Persist: load summary['judges'], set summary['judges'][name]['clarity'] = {alpha, alpha_metric, threshold: 0.67, meets_threshold: bool|None, n_cases, n_total_candidates, selection: 'all'|'stratified', seed, raters, n_raters, families, cross_family (True|False|None), incumbent_included} and rewrite via _merge_summary(run_id, 'judges', ...) — inside the judges block so report/regression consumers see it (V3-2 correction 1); full case × rater matrix under _merge_summary(run_id, 'clarity', {judge: {'cases': {case_id: {rater: value|None}}}}) for drill-down. config_surface:
judges:
  - name: task_quality
    llm_rubric: "Rate the response quality..."
    score_range: [1, 5]
    samples: 3                    # k draws PER panel model (k x m calls per case)
    model:                        # LIST = judge panel (string stays valid, unchanged)
      - claude-sonnet-4-5         # primary family
      - gpt-4o                    # gateway alias via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (LiteLLM /v1/messages)
      - gemini-2.5-pro            # >= 2 recognized families => "cross-family" label
  - name: format_check
    llm_rubric: "Output follows the required format"
    feedback_type: bool
    model: [claude-haiku-4-5, gpt-4o-mini, gemini-2.5-flash]   # odd size: bool ties resolve to fail

thresholds:
  task_quality:
